text:
maya: Quick heads-up — saw a p99 regression on the long-context workload after last night's kernel-selector change. p50/p95 barely moved but p99 jumped ~220ms for requests with input_len ~980-1050.

sam: Oof. Any obvious root cause from the flamegraphs?

maya: Profiler points at kernel selection flipping to the generic attention implementation for that sequence range. The selector's heuristics treat ~1024 as 'edge case' and falls back. Patch lowered microbatch to 16 and that made queuing worse. Logs: 
```
[profile] req=abc123 seq_len=1002 microbatch=16 kernel=generic_attn time=420ms
[profile] req=abc124 seq_len=998 microbatch=8 kernel=fast_qkv time=85ms
[profile] backend_queue_depth=18
```

lee: Hmm. Two levers: make selector prefer fast_qkv for 960-1056 if quant params match, or adjust microbatching so those requests don't hit the high tail.

dario: Also noticed KV cache churn is spiking for the same cohort. Evictions cause full recompute for some tokens which amplifies tail. Eviction metric: cache_miss_after_eviction spikes by 12x during the period.

sam: Could be a compound effect — fallback kernel + cache miss = huge tail. What do we want to try first?

maya: Proposal: 1) short-term safety net = soft max_tokens cap for requests when queue_depth>12 (progressive truncation). 2) medium = tweak kernel selector threshold for that seq range. 3) instrument sampled requests for quality regression.

lee: Agree. For (1) we can implement a config like: 
```json
{"adaptive_truncation": {"queue_threshold": 12, "max_tokens_floor": 32, "decay_ms": 3000}}
```
When queue_depth > queue_threshold we enforce max_tokens = min(request.max_tokens, computed_floor) and respond with metadata hint so caller knows.

dario: +1. On cache side we can change eviction policy to prefer keeping keys from active sessions (LRU + session_affinity boost). That should reduce recompute for long convs.

rachel: What about quality impact? Some customers rely on full completions. We need canary and metrics for semantic drift.

maya: Canary plan: roll adaptive_truncation to 1% traffic in prod for 6 hours, monitor p99, p95, token burn, and eval on held prompt set with BLEU/embedding similarity sampling. If similarity drop > 1.5% we rollback.

sam: Good. Also add a kernel-selector AB: keep old selector for 1% and new for 1% to measure diff. We need to measure end-to-end latency and rerun the tail-latency profiler.

lee: Implementation checklist: 
- kernel-selector: add fast_qkv preferred range override for seq_len in [960,1056]
- runtime: add adaptive_truncation middleware that reads queue_depth and request.max_tokens
- cache: bias eviction for active session ids
- telemetry: add trace tags "truncation_applied" and "kernel_override"

dario: I can do the cache eviction change and add the trace tag for cache_miss_after_eviction.

maya: I'll own the adaptive_truncation middleware + canary rollout. Sam, can you own the kernel-selector tweak?

sam: Yep. I'll add a small threshold param and feature-flag it behind ff/runtime.kernel_override_1024. Will also add unit tests to ensure no performance cliff for shorter seqs.

deploy-bot: deploy started: maya/adaptive-truncation canary -> staging (build 4821)

rachel: For observability, please add dashboards: p99 latency by seq_len bucket (0-256,256-512,512-768,768-960,960-1056,1056+), cache_eviction_rate, truncation_applied_ratio.

maya: Will add dashboards and a log-sampling policy: sample 1% of truncated requests and store full input+output in secure logs for quality review.

lee: One more thought — instead of hard truncation, consider progressive token shedding: when queue grows, prefer truncating trailing system messages or reducing planning tokens first. Less user-visible. Add as follow-up if canary shows too much drift.

sam: good note. We'll include a fallback param in the middleware: 
```json
{"prefer_system_trim": true}
```

dario: Also put a KV warming pass for sessions that are about to be evicted if they look high-value (heuristic: recent_req_count>10 && avg_resp_len>200). That should reduce cold recompute storms.

maya: Timeline: implement in staging today, run load test with synthetic long-context workload tomorrow morning, canary in prod after green load tests. I'll post perf comparisons here once we have numbers.

rachel: Thanks — please @me in the canary alert channel.

sam: Thx. If anyone runs into a regression, revert the selector FF immediately.

maya: ack. starting PRs now. :raised_hands:

lee: cheers. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: maya/adaptive-truncation canary -> staging (build 4821)

maya: staging perf smoke: p99 down 180ms on targeted bucket with microbatch=8 in the test harness. Will run longer runs next.

sam: Nice. Post the flamegraphs when ready.

maya: Will do. End of thread for now.
